Metabolic and skeletal complications of HIV infection: the price of success. JAMA 2006; 296: 844–54. HIV-associated malignancies. There is an increased incidence of certain malignancies in patients with HIV in- fection. Malignancies commonly associated with HIV in- fection are Kaposi’s sarcoma (p.675), Hodgkin’s disease, non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma and primary CNS lymphoma (see AIDS-related Lymphomas, p.657), invasive cervical cancer (p.663), and anal cancer (see Malignant Neoplasms of the Anus, p.666). Some tumours may regress in re- sponse to effective antiretroviral therapy. Guidelines for the management of HIV-associated malignancies have been issued by the British HIV association.1 1.
